plan: This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no incentive to bid above or below my true value of $35. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value.

This is a second-price auction, so the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value of $32. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth if the second-highest bid exceeds my value, while bidding lower reduces my chances of winning without any benefit, since I only pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid. Bidding my true value maximizes my expected profit given the auction mechanics.

Since I win and pay the second-highest bid if I have the highest bid, there's no incentive to bid above or below my true value of $48. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever profitable (when my value exceeds others' bids) and never overpay (since I'd only pay what the second-highest bidder bid, which would be less than my value in a winning scenario).
